Occlusion study · proposed architecture · 30 Sep 2026

SAM 3 with identity recovery

The official SAM 3 and SAM 3.1 architectures as published by Meta, and where our module attaches. The diagnosis showed that identity is lost when a person reappears after an occlusion and is given a new ID. In SAM 3 that decision is made in one place: the step that merges new detections with the objects already being tracked.

Official architectures figures from the SAM 3 paper and code release

Our redraw: SAM 3 plus identity recovery same colour scheme as the official figure; the ⊕ is opened up

Reading. Everything in teal, blue and yellow is SAM 3 as released; numbers are the settings used in our benchmark runs. Association matches detections to tracked masklets on mask overlap only. A masklet that stays unmatched is deleted once its keep-alive runs out (up to 30 frames), and a detection that matches nothing and scores ≥ 0.7 becomes a new object with a new ID. Our module (purple) intercepts that branch and first asks whether the detection is someone we recently lost.

What changes

ComponentSAM 3 as releasedWith identity recovery
Association cueMask overlap with a live masklet (IoU ≥ 0.1)Overlap, plus predicted position (motion) and appearance similarity
Objects that disappearMasklet and its memory deleted when keep-alive expiresKept in a lost-track gallery for T seconds: last mask and box, velocity, appearance embedding
Unmatched detectionNew ID if score ≥ 0.7Matched against the gallery first; new ID only if no candidate passes the motion gate and similarity ≥ τ
Appearance sourceNot used for identityPerception Encoder features averaged under the object's mask; no new network (a re-ID network is the fallback)
Trainingnone needed for our use (zero-shot)none; T, τ and the gate are tuned on sequences that are not scored
Where in codeSam3VideoBase._associate_det_trk()Level 1: a causal layer on SAM's per-frame output. Level 2: a hook in the new-detection branch of _associate_det_trk()

Two levels of integration

Level 1: outside SAM (first experiment)

Runs frame by frame on SAM's outputs and only relabels IDs, using past frames only, so it works online. SAM's code and weights are untouched, and it can be evaluated on the tracker outputs we already have with the same TrackEval and occlusion metrics.

Level 2: inside SAM

The same decision placed in the new-detection branch of the association step. A recovered object also gets its saved memory back (dashed line), so the tracker continues from its history instead of starting from an empty memory. In SAM 3.1 this means writing back into a multiplexed memory bucket, which is harder; we target SAM 3 first.

Success criteria. Higher identity recovery R through occlusion (especially ≥ 2 s, where SAM 3 keeps 73%), higher AssRe and AssA, and no increase in merges (AssPr must not fall), measured with official TrackEval and the occlusion protocol used in the diagnosis.
